page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.sn2.3xlarge is a general-purpose virtual machine based on KVM virtualization and powered by the x86_64 Intel Xeon 8269CY processor clocked at 2.5 GHz. The instance configuration allocates 16 dedicated vCPUs spanning 8 physical cores with two threads per core, backed by 35 MB of shared L3 cache and supported by vector instruction sets including AVX-512 and AVX-512 VNNI. Memory capacity is provisioned at 64.0 GB, maintaining a balanced 1:4 CPU-to-memory ratio of 4.0 GB per vCPU. Networking operates with a 3 Gbps baseline bandwidth, while the instance features no bundled local storage and includes zero GPUs.

Benchmark results demonstrate consistent mid-tier performance across multi-threaded applications alongside weaker single-core processing capabilities. The instance yields an average multi-core CPU score of 11798.08 in stress-ng and 6324.0 in Geekbench, contrasting with weak single-thread performance indicators such as a Geekbench single-core score of 1001.0 and single-threaded gzip compression at 19.04 GB/sec. Memory operations show robust uncached bandwidth metrics, delivering 75.86 GB/sec for large-block reads and 55.65 GB/sec for large-block writes, complemented by a Redis throughput of 11.35 million SET operations per second.

The hardware profile emphasizes multi-threaded concurrency rather than single-threaded speed. Cost efficiency is balanced for tasks that utilize the full 16 vCPU spread and steady memory allocations, though environments dependent on extreme per-core clock speed or ultra-fast decompression may find the processor architecture limiting. With no integrated local storage or complimentary public IPv4 addressing, additional external block storage is necessary for persistent storage requirements.

The ecs.sn2.3xlarge is suitable for general-purpose server workloads requiring balanced CPU and memory allocation. Recommended deployments include relational and in-memory database instances, multi-threaded static web serving, intermediate microservices clusters, batch processing jobs, and modest small-model machine learning inference tasks.
